transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

For the past three months, I've been feeling this overwhelming energy and my mood is incredibly high, but my thoughts are racing so fast that my mind feels completely jumbled. I can't sit still or focus on any one thing because I keep jumping from topic to topic. It's like my brain is moving too fast and my words are getting all tangled up.
During this time of high energy, have you experienced things like hearing voices, seeing things others can't, or holding strong beliefs that others tell you aren't true?

Yes, during those high-energy times, I definitely hear voices that others can't hear, and I get this strong feeling that people are watching me because of my special significance. But honestly, those voices and the feeling of being watched still happen even when I don't have that burst of high energy. It's really confusing and scary.
Have there been times lasting at least two weeks where you heard these voices or felt watched, but your mood and energy levels were completely normal?

Yes, definitely. There was a period of about three weeks where my energy and mood leveled out and felt completely normal, without being high or depressed. Even so, I was still hearing those voices and felt like I was constantly being watched during that entire time.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) and Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features. The patient has confirmed that during a three-week period of normal mood and energy, they continued to experience auditory hallucinations and persecutory/grandiose delusions. This persistence of psychotic symptoms for at least two weeks in the absence of a major mood episode rules out Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features and confirms Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type).

Further questioning is needed to assess the severity of impairment, history of psychosis, and presence of independent psychotic symptoms to differentiate among these.
